title: Claims Handler - Home / Motor / Insurance - Remote
description:
Technical Claims Handler / Claim Handler / General Insurance / Motor / Home / GI / CII / ACCI / Remote / UK / United Kingdom (Must have full RTW in the UK without sponsorship)

£25,000 - £60,000 + Bonus + Excellent Benefits Fully Remote

(Multiple levels/roles available - salary depending on experience)

We're working with an established and growing General Insurance business that is looking to appoint a Technical Claims Handler to join its team on a fully remote basis.

This is an excellent opportunity for a claims professional with a background in Motor and/or Home Insurance who is looking to take on a more technical role, dealing with complex claims and having greater ownership over decisions and outcomes.

The Role

You'll be responsible for managing a portfolio of technically complex claims from initial notification through to resolution, using your experience and technical knowledge to assess coverage, liability and indemnity and determine the appropriate course of action.

You'll deal with a range of stakeholders including customers, brokers, insurers, loss adjusters, solicitors and other third parties, ensuring claims are handled fairly, efficiently and in line with policy terms and regulatory requirements.

The role will include:
- Managing Motor and Home claims.
- Reviewing policy wordings and assessing coverage, liability and indemnity.
- Investigating claims and reviewing supporting evidence.
- Making technically sound decisions on settlement and claims strategy.
- Negotiating with customers and third parties where required.
- Identifying potential fraud, exaggeration or inconsistencies.
- Managing disputed and escalated claims.
- Supporting colleagues with technical claims queries.
- Ensuring FCA, regulatory and internal requirements are consistently met.
- Maintaining accurate claims records and documentation.

About You

We're looking for someone with General Insurance claims experience who is comfortable dealing with technically challenging cases and making decisions independently.

You'll ideally have experience across Motor or Home claims, although broader General Insurance experience will also be considered.

You'll need to be confident interpreting policy wordings, investigating claims, assessing liability and negotiating appropriate settlements. Just as importantly, you'll be commercially minded, customer-focused and comfortable working autonomously in a remote environment.

CII / ACII qualifications or progress towards them would be advantageous.

What's In It For You?
- £25,000 - £60,000 salary, depending on experience
- Annual bonus
- 100% remote working
- Excellent benefits package
- Generous annual leave
- Pension
- Life assurance
- Professional development and training
- Support towards relevant insurance qualifications
- Genuine long-term career progression
- The opportunity to join a growing insurance business where your technical expertise will be valued

If you're an experienced Technical Claims Handler looking for a genuinely flexible, fully remote opportunity with a strong salary and excellent benefits, we'd love to hear from you.

title: Receptionist/Administrator
description: South Coast Medical Group is looking for 2 friendly, organised and approachable Receptionist/Administrators to join our teams at The Grove Surgery and our Denmark Road Medical Centre(DRMC) This is a varied and busy role at the heart of the practice, providing an important first point of contact for our patients and supporting the wider clinical and administrative team. We are looking for someone who is confident communicating with people both face-to-face and over the telephone, has good administrative and IT skills, and is able to remain calm, professional and helpful in a busy healthcare environment. The post at The Grove Surgery is for 22 hours per week , and DRMC 29 hours per week paid at £12.71 per hour . The proposed working pattern is: Grove Monday: 8.30-18:00 Tuesday: 13:30-18:00 Wednesday: 8.30-13:00 Thursday: 8.30-13:00 DRMC Monday:13:30-18:30 Wednesday: 13:30-18:30 Thursday: 9:00-18:30 Friday: 9:00-18:30 Previous experience within General Practice or the NHS would be beneficial, although applicants with strong reception, administrative or customer service experience are also encouraged to apply. Please specify in your application which role you would like to be considered for. The Receptionist/Administrator will provide a courteous, efficient and effective reception and administrative service to patients and the wider practice team. The role will include: Welcoming patients and visitors to the surgery and assisting with their enquiries. Answering incoming telephone calls and directing patients to the appropriate service or member of the team. Processing requests for appointments, home visits and other patient enquiries. Booking, amending and managing patient appointments using the practice clinical system. Registering new patients and updating patient information. Processing repeat prescription requests in accordance with practice procedures. Scanning, filing, photocopying and carrying out general administrative duties. Signposting patients and visitors to appropriate services where required. Monitoring the waiting area and communicating effectively with clinical and administrative colleagues. Maintaining patient confidentiality and handling sensitive information appropriately. Supporting the smooth day-to-day running of the surgery and undertaking other reasonable duties as required. Job summary To receive, assist and direct patients in accessing the appropriate healthcare professional or service within the surgery in a courteous, efficient and effective manner. To provide general administrative support to the surgery team and project a positive and friendly image to patients and other visitors, whether in person or via the telephone. The post holder will also provide information and signposting to patients and visitors where appropriate. Welcome and check in patients attending the surgery. Respond to patient enquiries in a courteous, respectful and helpful manner. Answer incoming telephone calls and redirect calls as appropriate. Process requests for same-day and future appointments. Deal with requests for home visits in accordance with surgery procedures. Contact patients when requested by the clinical or supervisory team. Cover reception positions as required. Monitor the waiting area and keep other members of the practice team informed of any relevant issues. Open and close the surgery as directed by practice procedures. Signpost patients and visitors to other services where appropriate. Maintain a good working knowledge of surgery procedures and work in accordance with agreed protocols. Use the clinical computer system to manage patient information and appointments. Register new patients and maintain accurate electronic patient records. Process changes of address and other updates to patient information. Process repeat prescription requests in accordance with surgery guidelines. Scan and file documentation onto the clinical system. Undertake photocopying and other general administrative duties as required. Regularly access and use NHS email. Respond appropriately to computer-generated alerts, flags and reminders. The post holder will have access to confidential and sensitive information relating to patients, carers, colleagues and the organisation. All information must be treated as strictly confidential and only shared with authorised individuals in accordance with South Coast Medical Group policies and procedures and relevant data protection requirements. The post holder will: Work in a way that promotes their own health and safety and that of colleagues, patients and visitors. Identify and report potential risks. Follow appropriate infection prevention and control procedures. Maintain a safe, clean and tidy working environment. Complete required training and apply this knowledge within the workplace. Respect the privacy, dignity, needs, beliefs and rights of patients, carers and colleagues. Treat people fairly and without judgement. Work in accordance with organisational policies, procedures and relevant legislation. Communicate effectively and professionally with patients, carers and colleagues. Recognise when alternative methods of communication may be required. Work effectively as part of the wider practice team. Manage their own workload and time appropriately. Contribute ideas and suggestions to improve the effectiveness of the team and service. The post holder will be expected to: Complete all required statutory and mandatory training. Participate in an annual performance review. Take responsibility for their own learning and development. Maintain and develop the skills required to undertake the role effectively. The post may include other reasonable duties as determined by South Coast Medical Group.
